symptom: Invalid input is accepted, or valid input is rejected with a 422 naming a field that looks correct.
cause: The generated validator is stale. It is produced from the validate tags on the request struct, so changing a tag without regenerating leaves the old rules in force — and hand-editing the generated file means the next regeneration silently reverts it.
steps: Confirm the request struct lives in handler/request/request.go (package request). Validators are generated only from there.
Run govalid_gen. It runs govalid ./request.go from the handler directory.
Run go_build: a regenerated validator referencing a renamed field fails to compile, which is the signal you want.
Never edit request_*_validator.go. The header says DO NOT EDIT and it means it.
watch_out: A struct with no validate tags generates no validator at all, so the endpoint accepts anything. An absent validator file is the symptom, not an omission.
